question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Have a bash
solution:
The correct answer is **"to make an attempt."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Have a bash"** is an idiom that means to try something. (कुछ प्रयास करना)

 
 
• **Example**:* I've never done it before, but I'll **have a bash**__ at it.*
 
 
 
• The word** "bash" **can also mean a party or celebration, but in this context, it means to attempt something.
 
• This idiom is commonly used in informal settings.
 
• It can be used in a positive or negative sense, depending on the context.
 
• The correct answer is Option 2.
